P1.evidence: Pre-call information acknowledged rather than read back — 'I already got some information, but I would just like to hear everything from you.' Frame was two-part with the fit test attached, missing what's-in-the-way and what-you-need. Agreement asked ('Sounds good?') and given. Open question ran: 'how is it going at the moment? What can we potentially help you with? Take me through it.'

P2.evidence: Height, weight and body fat all asked directly — 'what do you weigh at the moment, and how tall are you?' and 'any estimate that you can put on your body fat?' — with a useful follow-up on fat distribution. Work and study both asked ('Do you work a lot?', 'what do you do for school?'). Pain was interrogated properly: duration, triggers, and impact on sleeping, driving, sitting and studying. Nutrition was the most detailed in the batch, down to calorie range, cheat-meal frequency and condiment habits. Gaps: no general health-conditions or hereditary question — the herniated disc was volunteered, and the recent military medical discharge was mentioned at minute 46 and never asked about at all; days trained per week never established; sleep quantity emerged only as a symptom of the pain rather than being asked; energy never asked.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in the batch. He did not accept the first surface answer and dug three times: 'I'm guessing no pain' became 'when you don't have that pain anymore, what does it sort of mean to you?' became 'why is it so important to you?' — which produced 'because living with pain is not life. And that's my motivation.' He then reflected it back and had it confirmed: 'your biggest why is just being able to move without feeling anything... is that correct?' — 'Correct, yeah, feel healthy.' The gap is the same one as everywhere else in this folder: no who-else-does-this-impact question, and no route to family or legacy even though a wife is mentioned.

P4.evidence: Asked whether he had worked with a trainer or online coach before, how it went, and then the phase's central question in a good form: 'what do you think this time is going to be different from all of the other times that you've already attended something?' The answer was substantive — previous approaches were running, abs work and CrossFit that he disliked, and bodybuilder-style coaches whose goals were not his. The rep drew the right conclusion out loud: 'before you didn't really like the sort of work that you were doing, and this time you actually like it.' What is missing is a hard blocker question and the information-isn't-the-problem move; the named gap stayed at enjoyment and technique rather than structure.

P5.evidence: Ran cleanly and produced the strongest answer of any call in the batch. 'Can you imagine yourself having that type of pain still when you're 40?' — 'Oh, yeah, no, that would suck.' Then the settle question, which the prospect asked him to repeat and then answered fully: 'No, not at all, because I know if I quit, it just gets worse... if I don't work out, I know there'll be a point where I can't even stand up.' The why-not arrived inside that answer without being asked separately. Only the line-in-the-sand ask is missing.

P6.evidence: P6a ran in full after the pillars — 'do you feel like when we get the training, mobility, nutrition, and also that lifelong success with Trevor in place, that you're going to be able to get to the goals?' — answered '100%'. A clear yes was in hand before the price was named, which is what the phase exists for. The all-in question was only approximated by asking which of the three elements would help most. The structural criticism belongs to the process rather than the rep: a full commitment was secured from a man who, forty minutes later, turned out to have $100 a month, because nothing in the sequence establishes capacity before the offer.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected; no link was sent and no plan was agreed. Steps two to four were unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete run of the money play in the batch. Isolate ran twice, including a good variant — asking him to rate the programme one to ten with the money set aside, which produced a genuine endorsement rather than a polite one. The worth test ran ('do you feel like that is worth $6,000 to you?' — 'Definitely'). Financial picture: cash available now ('even if it's five bucks, just be completely honest with me'), monthly surplus ($100), and credit score (780). Then a structure was proposed, $500 a month over twelve months. Not run: the permission ask before opening the financial conversation, number of credit cards, available credit, used versus available, and investments. Two judgement notes — the rep correctly did not touch money the prospect had earmarked for rent and bills, and he did not discount, which is the opposite of what he did on four other calls in this batch.

A clear not-the-right-time trigger at 00:46:31 — 'this year, I see it impossible. I would say next year.' No move ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. Recorded as a miss for consistency, but flagged as the right call: the prospect had just disclosed a medical discharge, $13,000-$14,000 of cleared arrears and a loan being taken to pay tuition. Running urgency there would have been the wrong thing to do, and the rep instead said 'the last thing that we would want to do is put you in a financial position'.

The clinical gap, again and at its most serious. A years-old herniated disc with pain severe enough to prevent sitting through classes, currently being treated by a doctor with myofascial release, in a man recently given a medical discharge from the military. There is no scripted step that says stop and obtain clearance, so instead the condition became the sales argument — 'that's also going to help stabilizing everything also for your herniated disc' and 'that's also how the pain actually stays away'.

notes: Process-wise the best call in the batch: real baseline numbers, goals dug three levels deep to 'living with pain is not life', a consequence frame that landed, a clear commitment before price, and a money play run properly without a discount. Two problems remain. Capacity is discovered only after forty minutes of work, which is a process design fault rather than a rep fault. And the clinical picture that made this prospect so motivated is exactly the one that should have paused the sale.
